text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe vows to cut income tax by some 25 billion francs over a five-year period, beginning in 1997 (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- Crude oil prices soar after U.S. launches missile raid on Iraq. Dollar strengthens, securities and bonds worldwide affected. Paris bourse closed slightly lower. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie registers an order for 32 airplanes, worth around 11 billion francs.
-- Italian businessman Carlo De Benedetti to step down as chairman of computer group Olivetti.
-- French authorities are reluctant to express support for U.S. President Bill Clinton's raid on Iraq.
-- Lagardere Groupe MMBP.PA chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere says he will disclose on September 15 whether his company is bidding for soon-to-be-privatised Thomson SA and on what terms.
-- Shoe manufacturer Bally France filed for bankruptcy yesterday.
-- Some 35 billion francs owed by France Telecom for civil servant retirements could be used to fill part of the French budget deficit to help meet the Maastricht treaty criteria.
-- U.S. hits Iraq with 27 missile strikes.
-- Airbus Industrie European consortium plans to build a jet capable of carrying nearly 1,000 people.
